answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring a verifiable history of useful work before an identity gains full rights. Like a ship that must dock at a wharf many times before it is trusted with cargo, a new agent starts at the bottom and earns standing only through a thread of completed, checkable tasks over days. Reaching the zenith of trust takes sustained effort, so an attacker who spawns a thousand fake identities must repeat that whole slow history for each one, making the attack far more expensive than the reward it could capture.
